bib.title: Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Recursive Experiential-Working Memory Evolution for Long-Horizon Agent Harnesses" (Recuris), Zhaochen Yu, Yingcheng Wu, Zhenfei Yin, Kaiyuan Chen, Zhe Zhao, Mengdi Wang, Shuicheng Yan, Ling Yang (NUS, Stanford, Oxford, Princeton). Preprint, arXiv:2608.24876v1 [cs.AI], 25 Aug 2026. Not peer reviewed.

COVERAGE: All 108,448 chars read, including appendices A-E. References were read but only skimmed for origins. Figure captions script returned nothing, so the figure information below comes from the text extraction only.

FIT WARNING (partial fit). This is not a study of raw versus distilled memory, and it does not test RAG or full-context baselines in the usual sense. "Experiential Memory (EM)" means a small library of distilled skills (10 skills for the retail champion). "Working Memory (WM)" means a verified task-state tracker. The closest baselines are "model-controlled" injection, where the whole skill library sits in the prompt every turn (a full-context analogue), and a base agent with no memory. There is no raw-trajectory memory arm and no embedding-RAG arm. The paper's own related work says that similarity retrieval over raw observations is what prior systems did, but it never runs that arm. Best use: distilled skills and when they are invoked, plus a cost row.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. Invocation control matters more than skill content. Putting the whole skill library in context costs more tokens, and scores below having no skills.
 number: 83.6 vs 65.6 task success; 147k vs 101k agent tokens per success; WM-only with no skills 82.0
 setup: tau2-Retail, 114 tasks, k=4 (456 episodes per variant), doubao-seed-2-0-pro. Variants are matched on model, decoding, harness and seeds. Model-controlled and Recuris carry the same 10 skills, byte-identical.
 quote: "Putting the whole library in context and delegating invocation to the model scores below the identical configuration carrying no skills at all,82.0, and costs more to run:147k agent tokens per success against101k for Recuris."
 where: Sec 3.3.4 and Table 3, p.16. Table 12 (App D) has the token detail.
2. Skills alone add little. A verified working state is what carries the gain.
 number: EM only +2.0 [-4.0,+7.9]; WM only +23.9 [+17.5,+30.3]; EM+WM +25.4
 setup: tau2-Retail, base 58.1% (265/456). Paired task-clustered bootstrap 95% CI.
 quote: "Against the base agent, adding experiential memory is worth +2.0points on τ2-Retail and+1.5on τ2-Airline, neither excluding zero, while adding a verified working state is worth+23.9."
 where: Sec 3.3.2, Table 2, p.14. On Airline (50 tasks) every CI includes zero, so the authors call it "a direction".
3. Memory distilled from failures transfers to held-out tasks and to other models. It does not help where the held-out set has no failures left to fix.
 number: +9.01 to +17.44 on 86 held-out tasks; M0 54.07 to M2 71.51. Cross-model: GPT-5.6 Sol 58.33 to 76.10, Claude Opus 5 72.37 to 87.94.
 setup: Memory evolved from 16 failed tasks (12 dev tasks gate it) on the mid-sized deployment model, then frozen. Held-out 86 tasks at k=4. Nothing is evolved at evaluation time.
 quote: "Memory evolved from sixteen failures raises success on eighty-six tasks it never saw, by nine to seventeen points"
 where: Sec 3.4.5, Table 5, p.18-21. Table 7, p.22.
4. Benefit is bounded by headroom. A near-zero effect of the bare layer, and gains on only some models.
 number: harness-only effect (M0 vs bare) is about 0 on four models; improvement in 35 of 37 pairs; Retail Claude Opus 5 +15.6, Airline +1.0; Gemini 3.7 Flash Retail +4.8, Airline -1.5
 setup: Table 1, avg@4, 10 models from 3B to frontier. Table 10/11 (App B) is Retail with 86-88 tasks per model.
 quote: "Recuris improves task success in 35 of the 37 completed model–benchmark pairs."
 where: Table 1, p.12; App B, p.31.
5. Test-time adaptation, where a memory is rewritten from one task's own failure, is mostly explained by the retry budget.
 number: +26.4 from retry alone; adaptation adds +2.3 (p=0.774)
 setup: Terminal-Bench 2.1, 87 tasks, 4 attempts, Terminus-2 and doubao-seed-2-0-pro. The control shares the first rollout.
 quote: "retrying the seed memory is worth the same+26.4points on its own, 23 tasks flipping to solved and none flipping back (p <10−4), while at a matched budget of four attempts adaptation adds+2.3points, 7 tasks won against 5 lost (p= 0.774)."
 where: Sec 3.5, Table 8, p.23-24. Per-attempt avg@4 is +4.5 (CI [-0.9,+9.8]) on the 56 tasks with a learned skill. The authors call this a direction only.
6. Structured traces localize faults far better than the outcome alone or the raw trajectory (a point about distilled versus raw evidence).
 number: macro accuracy 13.0 (outcome), 37.0 (raw trajectory), 64.8 (structured trace); chance floor 33.3
 setup: Injected faults in 3 of 4 components, 54 verdicts per condition, fixed LLM judge.
 quote: "Macro accuracy is13.0%from the outcome,37 .0%from the raw trajectory and64.8%from Γ (table 4)"
 where: Sec 3.4.1, Table 4, p.17-18.
Other numbers worth keeping:
- Memory grew but was not fragile: 8 accepted patches added 51 skills, revised 2, deprecated 0; removing the 5 procedure skills moved the result by -2.3 to +1.7 (Sec 3.4.4).
- The gate rejected two candidates that later gained +11.92 on held-out tasks; the 12-task dev split gave a CI over 30 points wide (App E).
- SkillFlow: one family went from 0/8 to 7/8 by swapping the procedure template. The selection is in-sample (Table 13).

BASELINES AND TOKEN MATCHING
- Baselines: (a) base reference agent with no memory; (b) Recuris with initial memory M0 (a neutral layer with no skills); (c) EM-only; (d) WM-only; (e) model-controlled (all skills injected every turn); (f) Recuris with evolved memory.
- Matched: model, tools, tasks, seeds, step budget and user simulator.
- Tokens are not matched by design. Table 12: first-call prompt 5,163 (bare), 5,636 (WM-only), 8,274 (model-controlled), 5,632 (Recuris). Tokens per episode 67,315 / 83,938 / 96,289 / 84,275; per success 115,833 / 102,341 / 146,849 / 100,865.
- The model-controlled arm gets more skill text, and the paper uses that to argue that availability is not the mechanism.
- Dollar cost is unavailable because cost fields are zero. Per-turn rendered memory tokens were not recoverable. Tokens were not aggregated for Terminal-Bench or SkillFlow. The cost of running the evolution loop (Meta-Agent) is never reported; the paper says only that evolution "is the expensive step".
- No RAG arm, no raw-history memory arm, and no long-context-only comparison beyond the injected-library arm.

LIMITS
- Authors concede: Airline results are directional only (50 tasks); run-to-run noise on Retail is about +/-7 points ("Re-running one τ2-Retail package unchanged... moves task success by +0.00points with an interval of [-6.98,+7.27]"). Terminal-Bench has no cross-task structure, and cross-task evolution admitted no patch in 13 runs. SkillFlow has no held-out task split, so it measures transfer across models and not across tasks. The checker ablation is inert on Retail. Run B's round 4 was never invoked, and Run C's round 4 gave back most of its gain. 17 near-duplicate skill pairs survived.
- Not shown: any comparison against an existing memory system such as ExpeL, AWM or Mem0; results from more than one deployment model; dollar cost.
- Many evaluated models are future-dated names and cannot be checked independently. Most gains are on tau2-Retail, which has shared policy structure, and the memory is evolved with a Claude Code-based Meta-Agent, which is a heavy setup.
- Table 1 mixes avg@4 across benchmarks; Terminal-Bench is avg@4 in Table 1 and solved-within-budget in Table 8.

BUILDS ON
Voyager (Wang, TMLR 2024); Agent Workflow Memory (Wang, ICML 2025); ExpeL (Zhao, AAAI 2024); Buffer of Thoughts (Yang, NeurIPS 2024); ReasonFlux (Yang 2025); Dynamic Cheatsheet (Suzgun, EACL 2026); Agent Skills format (Anthropic 2025); ReasoningBank (Ouyang, ICLR 2026); Memento (Zhou 2025); Mem0 (Chhikara 2025); A-MEM (Xu, NeurIPS 2025); Reflexion (Shinn, NeurIPS 2023); GEPA (Agrawal, ICLR 2026); DSPy (Khattab, ICLR 2024); AutoGuide (Fu, NeurIPS 2024); SGDR (Li 2026a); StateAct (Rozanov & Rei, 2025); ReflAct (Kim, EMNLP 2025); Magentic-One (Fourney 2024); StructAgent (Wu 2026); Godel machine (Schmidhuber 2003); Darwin Godel Machine (Zhang 2025b); tau2-Bench (Barres 2025); SkillFlow (Zhang 2026c); Terminal-Bench (Shaw 2026).

CODE: none.

FIGURES (one candidate): Fig 5 / Table 2 (p.14), "Coupling of EM and WM". Bars show gain over the base agent for EM only (+2.0), WM only (+23.9) and EM+WM (+25.4) on tau2-Retail. It shows at a glance that skills alone barely help. Alternative: Table 12 (p.33) for the cost row.
